data.narrative:
Extropic is a Series A-stage semiconductor company founded by Guillaume Verdon and Trevor McCourt. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 private peers in Chips & Semiconductors (including SambaNova, Cerebras, PsiQuantum, Etched, and Tenstorrent) alongside three public benchmarks (ALAB, NVDA, AMD). The company has raised $50M+ to date.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable valuation lens, given insufficient density in narrow peer cohorts. Using total raised ($50M) as a base proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A progression yields an implied valuation of $100M. A peer-median approach was not viable; while 11 same-sector peers exist in the dataset, filtering for stage-matching or valuation-tier similarity yielded fewer than three datapoints, rendering sector-wide median comparison unreliable.

The triangulated range is $85M (low) to $115M (high), with a median of $100M. This single-method result carries material uncertainty. Key sensitivities include actual Series A-to-next-stage step-up multiples within the semiconductor subsector, market conditions affecting downstream funding velocity, and the absence of tighter peer comparables. Investors should require direct comps analysis or revenue/burn metrics to tighten confidence intervals.
